perturbed_required_facts: Under § 217.45(a)(1), an originating Board-regulated institution may treat a guarantee obtained to hedge exposure in a synthetic securitization as a recognized credit risk mitigant only if the synthetic securitization meets the operational requirements of § 217.41.

To satisfy § 217.41(b)(1)(ii), the guarantee must satisfy every element of the § 217.2 definition of an eligible guarantee other than criterion (3); the guarantee described here likely misses the required prompt-payment element because it allows a 90-day response period.

Since that prompt-payment defect means the guarantee is not an eligible guarantee within the meaning of § 217.2, § 217.41(b)(1)(ii) is not satisfied, so the institution may not recognize the guarantee for risk-based capital treatment as a credit risk mitigant.

Apart from the guarantee issue, the securitization also runs afoul of § 217.41(a)(4) because the pool contains revolving facilities under which borrowers can change drawn amounts within committed limits, and the structure includes an early amortization trigger.

When § 217.41(a)(4) is not met, the institution cannot exclude the underlying exposures from risk-weighted assets, must instead hold capital against them as though they were not securitized, and must deduct any after-tax gain-on-sale from common equity tier 1 capital.

The § 217.2 eligible-guarantee definition also matters outside this securitization analysis, because it is incorporated into the counterparty credit risk rules in § 217.132, including the standardized approach for OTC derivatives and repo-style transactions.
